answer: Registration runs through a clock-fingerprint gate. Each new identity ships a secure element; the node samples its oscillator twice, twelve hours apart, matching drift to two parts per million. The same silicon yields the same curve, so a farm running 200 clones reads as one identity; the other 199 slots are slashed. Cloning costs $40 per element; 10,000 fake accounts burn $400,000 and still fail sample two. Proof grows like a glacier cutting stone, a raven returning to one cliff, a vine climbing one wall: slow, repeated contact.
